display.title: Episode 324: The Flickering Flame (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show without music: respect and Ahavas Yisroel, why counting the Omer teaches the value of time, a young guest's Shema, and a shoemaker's lamp that teaches about teshuvah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 2 Iyar 5748, during Sefiras HaOmer, so the show opens without music. Uncle Yossi recalls the plague among Rabbi Akiva's students, who did not show each other respect, and lists the kinds of respect we can practice: for parents, for teachers and between friends, looking for the good in others and seeking peace. Ahavas Yisroel and achdus are the answer to 'Ad masai', and soldiers of Tzivos Hashem should set the example. He then explains that counting the Omer is counting time, Hashem's precious gift, which cannot be bought or recovered, illustrated by the story of a girl who keeps crying over a lost dime. A boy of almost five visits Studio 604 to lead the Shema and tells what he learns in cheder. Story time is 'The Flickering Flame': caught in a snowstorm, a great tzaddik named Rabbi Yisroel finds shelter with an old shoemaker who worked late because his lamp still burned, and draws the lesson that as long as the light burns, one can still repair. The show closes with a tour of the Pesach newsletter and an invitation to the Lag BaOmer parade.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: as long as the light still burns, we can still repair, so fill every day with Torah, mitzvos and respect for others.
